For example, when K = Z12, a solution to (a, b, c, d) is (4, 3, 3, 4).

candidates.statement: It is interesting to study the representations of free braid groups when K as a ring has zero divisors or is noncommutative, and then use it to study quantum invariants for free knots and links. Other possible ways of constructing free knot invariants may consist of constructing biquandles similar to [1, 4]. References [1] A. Bartholomew and R. Fenn, Quaternionic invariants of virtual knots and links, arXiv: math/0610484. [2] L. H. Kauﬀman, S. Lambropoulou, Virtual braids, Fundamenta Mathematicae 184 (2004), 159–186. [3] L. H. Kauﬀman, S. Lambropoulou, Virtual braids and the L-Move, Knot Theory and Its Ramiﬁcations J. 15 (2006), no. 6, 773–81

candidates.statement: For every n, the map SIn : VK →SGPn deﬁned for all K ∈VK by: SIn(K) = πn[ΣK] ◦In[ΣK](τK) is a Vassiliev invariant of virtual knots of degree ≤n. We show an example which proves that the invariant is non-trivial. Moreover, the groups SGPn are not isomorphic to the Polyak groups of [11].
